title: Update: ForgeSkills went from 20 to 28 skills. The agent has to judge the game before it builds anything
author: Fine-Reflection-7530
selftext:
Last time I posted this, ForgeSkills was 20 reusable skills for AI coding agents. The problem was the same one: an agent will call a game task finished when the result is still visibly wrong, or when nobody has tested it.

It is 28 skills now. Still procedures with a gate, still not "make it look better."

What got added:

Should this game exist. Two skills run before anyone models a tree. One asks what you can actually finish (people, months, engine, what you refuse to make), looks at shipped games, and comes back with one loop plus one twist. The other opens store pages, writes down the price, the review count, and a real complaint with the date, then says BUILD, NARROW, or STOP. A score has to be tagged as something you observed or something you inferred. Liking the theme is not evidence.

A boss is a timeline, then an animation. Each attack is a row: windup, the frames that can actually hurt, recovery, range, and a ban on using the same move three times in a row. Lock-on has to keep facing the target while you walk backward, or it does not ship. Juice comes after that timeline passes.

Audio is wiring. You pick the sounds. The skill hooks them to events that already exist, writes the license down, and checks that muting one bus makes a specific decision worse. It does not compose music.

The render is allowed to fail. Skills for a Godot scene that still looks like the default, foliage that reads as paper, and visual bugs you isolate instead of hiding (shimmer, shadow acne, z-fighting). Scripted Blender versus driving one live Blender session is a measured choice now.

The loop did not change:

Measure → Build → Render → Compare → Fix one thing → Repeat

The README opens on that loop. It starts at 0.46. That is a real silhouette score from this repo, against a gate of 0.85. The character never passed. I left the failure in the docs. A page that only shows wins is the same problem as an agent that says "looks good."

All 28 descriptions together are about 1,560 tokens, which is what the agent sees before it picks a skill. The long tables stay in separate files until a step asks for them.

Still Apache-2.0: [https://github.com/sekaikx/ForgeSkills](https://github.com/sekaikx/ForgeSkills)

And Thanks For your support

comments.body: Dude.. you're steering texels and wraparound? Foliage alpha controls... JFC.. that's cool. Thank you.

comments.author: thecrownforge
comments.body: does the same agent build the scene and decide if it passes? i would want a fresh check that only sees the target and the result, otherwise it might judge its own work too kindly. i would also try a few results with known problems, like a missing object or a wrong colour, and see if the check catches them. leaving the failed character in the docs helps, but knowing what the check misses would be useful too
